name: Io
tagline: Jupiter's volcanic moon — the most geologically active body in the Solar System.
history: Io is squeezed by Jupiter's gravity and the resonant pulls of Europa and Ganymede — the tidal flexing heats its interior until sulfur rock melts outright. Over four hundred active volcanoes paint the surface in yellows, oranges and blacks, and plumes like Pele's rise 300 km into space. Galileo saw it in 1610 as a mere point; Voyager 1 revealed the eruptions in 1979, the Galileo orbiter mapped the lava fields, and Juno now images its poles. Io's constant resurfacing means it has no visible craters — a young, violent face re-painted every few years.
